sources.citation: Mortensen, David R. 2021. East Tusom: a phonetic and phonological sketch of a largely undocumented Tangkhulic language. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area (author preprint, 8 pp. + appendices).
sources.note: About East Tusom (India), not Akyaung Ari, which is never mentioned. Family-level line, preprint p. 14: 'East Tusom, like other Tangkhulic languages, has non-contrastive stress that is predictable from weight and morphological factors (which are confounded).. Roots are simply long (bimoraic) and stressed while prefixes are short (monomoraic) and unstressed'; general pattern /LˈH/ (iambic) or /LLˈH/; three tones H, L, HL.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2011. Change Request 2011-020: create [nqy] Naga, Akyaung Ari (submitted 2010-12-07 by the Ethnologue editor; adopted 2012-02-03). Dallas: SIL International. 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Only content: a 436-item wordlist from Ngachan village collected by Myanmar researchers in 2004 shows 52% lexical similarity with Somra Tangkhul, 31% with Ukhrul Tangkhul, 23% with Koki Naga; 'because of local sensitivities, the publication of this document has been delayed'; no published sources listed.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2011. Request for New Language Code Element in ISO 639-3: nqy (companion form to CR 2011-020). 3 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Names (autonym Akyaung Ari; alt. Ngachan), three villages Heinkut, Jagram, Ngachan in southern Layshi Township, <1,000 speakers, 'no written literature, inscriptions or recordings', classification Kuki-Chin-Naga unclassified, closest to Somra Tangkhul; 'Knowledge from published sources' left blank.
